flags.estimate: count = 10 and 5 ROUNDS (trigger pulls), i.e. ~1.1 and ~0.55 magazines of her 9-ammo SG
flags.reasoning: Kit says 'normal attack(s)'. Per the round convention a round is one bullet = 1 per trigger pull (hitsPerShot only equals rounds for an MG); this SG's hitsPerShot 10 is PELLETS and the ammo economy spends 1/pull. If the engine's hitCount instead counts pellet impacts, both blocks fire ~10x too often — the 675% rider would land every half-pull, a large over-credit that no kit text supports.
flags.recipe: Read sim.ts's hitCount accumulator for weapon SG (does it add 1 per shot or hitsPerShot per shot?), then confirm empirically: run the control comp with an onEvent counter over damage events with bucket=rider/srcSlot=brid and compare the proc count against shots fired ÷ 5. Cross-check against footage popup cadence (a 675% popup should appear roughly once per ~5 shots, not ~once per shot).

flags.estimate: Use the datamined SG tuple as-is; effective pulls/sec = 60/ceil(60/nominal). No fire rate was supplied in this packet, so the shot cadence is entirely unverified here.
flags.reasoning: ALWAYS-⚑: rate_of_fire and reloadFrames are known-unreliable datamine fields, and BOTH skill2 blocks are cadence-driven — the every-5 675% rider's DPS contribution is linear in shots/sec, and reload downtime (111f ≈ 1.85s per 9 rounds) directly sets how many procs fit in a fight. A 20% cadence error is a ~20% error on this unit's rider damage.
flags.recipe: Confirm shots/sec with the instrument that measures it directly — the ammo counter in a recording (rounds drained per second), not FB counts. Cross-check reload duration frame-by-frame from magazine-empty to refill, and pin the result in docs/probe-runs.md before tuning any magnitude.

Writing crit:true explicitly would hardcode a convention that lives in the engine; writing crit:false would contradict it. Omission is the faithful choice but leaves the behaviour dependent on a global gate this blind read cannot inspect.
